from_quote: one member for every thirty thouſand perſons
rationale: The paragraph discusses the rate of one member for every thirty thousand persons and the provision that no state shall have less than one member, both of which are in Article I, Section 2, Clause 3.

from_quote: two years are the conſtitutional term of their exiſtence
rationale: The paragraph gives two years as the constitutional term of the representatives, as Article I, Section 2, Clause 1 does.

from_quote: the wiſdom of the Convention has propoſed an abſolute incapacity till the age of twenty-five
rationale: The paragraph names the age of twenty-five and the requirement that a representative be an inhabitant of his state, both of which are in Article I, Section 2, Clause 2.
to_quote: attained to the Age of twenty five Years

from_quote: With us, no placeman can ſit among the repreſentatives of the people
rationale: The paragraph says no "placeman" can sit among the representatives, which is the bar on holding office under the United States while a member in Article I, Section 6, Clause 2.
to_quote: no Person holding any Office under the United States, shall be a Member of either House

from_quote: The houſe of Repreſentatives is not, as the ſenate, to have a Preſident choſen for them from without their body
rationale: The paragraph contrasts the Senate's President, chosen from outside the body, with the House; the Senate's presiding officer is provided in Article I, Section 3, Clause 4.
to_quote: The Vice President of the United States shall be President of the Senate

from_quote: are to elect their Speaker from their own number
rationale: The paragraph says the representatives elect their Speaker, appoint their other officers and hold "the sole and uncontroulable power of impeachment," all of which are in Article I, Section 2, Clause 5.
to_quote: chuse their Speaker and other Officers

from_quote: they are to meet at leaſt once in every year
rationale: The paragraph says the representatives are to meet at least once in every year, the wording of Article I, Section 4, Clause 2.
to_quote: The Congress shall assemble at least once in every Year

from_quote: Should they differ in opinion, the Preſident, who is a temporary fellow-ſervant, and not their hereditary maſter, has a mediatorial power to adjuſt it for them
rationale: The paragraph says the President has a "mediatorial power" when the two houses differ, which describes his power to adjourn them when they disagree on the time of adjournment in Article II, Section 3.
to_quote: in Case of Disagreement between them, with Respect to the Time of Adjournment, he may adjourn them to such Time as he shall think proper

from_quote: The vote of each repreſentative can be always known, as well as the proceedings of the houſe
rationale: The paragraph says each representative's vote and the proceedings of the house can always be known, which describes the journal and the record of yeas and nays in Article I, Section 5, Clause 3.
to_quote: the Yeas and Nays of the Members of either House on any question shall, at the Desire of one fifth of those Present, be entered on the Journal

from_quote: for there is to be a perfect liberty of ſpeech
rationale: The paragraph says members are not to be restrained in their language because "there is to be a perfect liberty of speech," which refers to the Speech or Debate provision of Article I, Section 6, Clause 1.
to_quote: for any Speech or Debate in either House, they shall not be questioned in any other Place

from_quote: They, alone, can originate bills for drawing forth the revenues of the union
rationale: The paragraph says the House alone can originate bills for drawing forth the revenues of the union, which is Article I, Section 7, Clause 1.
to_quote: All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives
